newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel trade and services revenue declines.
newsitem.headline: Israel trade and services revenue declines.

text.p: Turnover in Israeli trade and services declined by an annualised 4.5 percent in the first three months of the year, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.

The bureau said that since the middle of 1996 turnover in trade and services has been falling month-to-month by an annualised rate of three percent, with decline sharpening to a 4.5 percent rate in January-March 1997.
The figures are based on data collected from a sample of value-added tax reports.
Despite the slowdown in the second half of 1996, activity in trade and services rose last year by 6.5 percent as a result of the activity growth in the first half of the year, the bureau said.

The slowdown affected all sectors but the sharpest fall was in financial services where turnover in the second half of 1996 fell by an annualised five percent. The decline sharpened to a six percent rate in the first quarter, the bureau said.

Activity in the food, trade and hotel sectors fell an average annualised three percent a month since the middle of 1996, but slowed slightly in first-quarter 1997 to an annualised 2.0 percent decline.
